title: Config Safety Signal Hub: Orchestrated Failsafe & Reconciliation
creator: Ethan Brooks
description: Background: We need an automated, conservative system for reverting problematic configuration changes (batching, caching, quantization flags, routing policies) across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments. Past incidents show single-metric triggers (latency > threshold) produce noisy reverts or oscillation. Proposal: implement a centralized 'Safety Signal Hub' that ingests multiple signals, computes a stability score, runs a pre-apply simulation, and only triggers staged reversion if confidence is high or safety windows are breached. The hub coordinates with the config-apply pipeline, the rollout controller, and the state-reconciliation service to ensure eventual consistency without flapping.
proposal_summary: 1) Multi-signal aggregation: latency P50/P95, error rate, token cost delta, tail GPU utilization, and model quality regressions (synthetic evals). 2) Stability score + hysteresis: compute an ephemeral score with cooling and heating windows to avoid oscillation. 3) Simulation pass: run a cheap simulation of new config on a small traffic shadow to predict cost/latency impact before commit. 4) Staged reverts: Canary rollback -> Region fallback -> Global rollback with automated mitigations and notifications. 5) Reconciliation: persistent state reconciler validates final desired state vs applied state and performs idempotent repair operations.
acceptance_criteria:
- Safety Signal Hub is deployed behind feature flag and receives metrics from telemetry pipeline.
- Stability score computed every 30s and stored to tracing/metrics backend.
- Simulation service runs for every config change and produces a predicted cost/latency delta; predictions are within 15% of observed for test traces.
- Automated revert triggers only after stability_score < 0.3 for 3 consecutive windows OR simulated rollback shows >10% improvement in a canary.
- Reconciliation loop repairs mismatches within 10 minutes and records an audit entry for each auto-action.
- Unit, integration, and chaos tests exist and pass in CI.
- Runbook and on-call alerting configured; stakeholders notified via Slack and e-mail for every auto-revert.

Implement stability_score service with hysteresis window and explainability fields
Add pre-apply simulation integration to config pipeline (shadow traffic harness)
Implement staged revert executor (canary/region/global) with rate-limited actions
Reconciliation loop: compare desired vs observed config state and repair conflicts

implementation_notes:
- Use Prometheus counters + histograms for latency and error signals; enrich with route/model tags.
- Token-cost delta computed from token counts + per-model unit cost; integrate pricing catalog service.
- Simulation will reuse existing shadowing infra but constrain sample sizes to keep cost < $X/day.
- Provide an 'explain' payload for each stability_score that includes top contributing signals for auditability.
- All auto-reverts must create a reversible change with comment, author='safety-hub', and link to the triggering signal window.
- For Private deployments, the hub emits signals but requires admin approval by default unless customer allows auto-revert via contract flag.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Conservative defaults: favor fewer false positives over faster reverts to avoid customer-facing oscillation
We accept potential lag in mitigation (up to configured hysteresis window) to reduce flaps
Simulation accuracy vs cost: initial window will use small sample traces and ML-based correction factors
Scope: will target config categories that historically cause outages first (batching, KV cache, routing). Quantization flags are lower priority until simulation fidelity improves
test_plan:
- Unit tests for stability_score math and hysteresis behavior.
- Integration: end-to-end test where synthetic metrics are injected and auto-revert is observed in a sandbox environment.
- Regression: run with historical incident traces and verify hub triggers match expected reverts.
- Chaos test: randomly flip config keys to ensure reconciliation repairs desired state.
- Load test: ensure hub handles 10k config changes/day without backpressure.
telemetry_and_alerting:
- New metrics: safety_hub.stability_score, safety_hub.explain.top_signals, safety_hub.actions{type,result}, safety_hub.simulation.predicted_delta.
- Alerts: P0 alert if auto-revert fails to execute or reconciliation loop stalls >10m.
- Slack channel: #safety-hub-alerts with threaded summaries and links to dashboard.
- Pager rotation: Eng oncall + SLA owner on call for any global rollback.
rollout_plan:
1) Canary: enable hub in 'observe-only' mode for 2 weeks to validate signals and scoring.
2) Shadow simulation: run simulation pass for live config changes and compare predicted vs observed for one week.
3) Soft-enable auto-actions for non-critical projects with small traffic (10% of changes). Monitor for 2 weeks.
4) Gradually increase scope and remove 'admin-approval' for Trusted Projects.
5) Full enable with audit logging and postmortem reviews for each auto-action.

open_questions: What is the canonical SLA for auto-revert notification windows to customers?
Should we allow customers to opt into 'aggressive auto-revert' if they prefer faster recovery at the risk of flaps?
How do we instrument model-quality regressions for black-box models where we only have sampled user feedback?
What budget cap should we enforce for daily simulation runs to bound platform cost?
